key_insight: Posterior Augmented Flow Matching supplements standard flow-matching training with posterior-derived supervisory signals to densify and lower-variance training, preventing collapse of learned transport maps on high-dimensional images.
problem_solved: Flow matching for high-dimension images suffers from extremely sparse, high-variance supervision (one trajectory per sample), causing flow collapse where diverse inputs map to similar outputs; this method addresses that under-constrained learning signal.
method: Estimate or sample posterior/conditional intermediate states between prior and data to create additional supervision along trajectories.
Augment flow-matching loss with these posterior-derived targets so each training sample supervises many intermediate points (denser, lower-variance gradients).
Train a time-dependent vector field using the augmented targets to learn stable, diverse transports that avoid memorized source–target pairings.
impact: Provides a practical way to stabilize and scale flow-matching to high-resolution image generation, improving sample diversity and reliability for practitioners building generative models.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: sparse single-trajectory supervision vs. dense posterior-augmented trajectories supervising the vector field.
Heatmap or bar chart showing training signal variance and collapse frequency before vs. after augmentation.
Grid of generated images comparing diversity and quality (baseline FM vs. posterior-augmented FM).
Flow-field visualization (arrows) showing smoother, non-collapsed transport learned with augmentation.
paper_authors: George Stoica, Sayak Paul, Matthew Wallingford, Vivek Ramanujan, Abhay Nori
